# strength_progress — research (generated by research.py; do not edit)

Question: given a lifter's log up to today, what will they lift at a future date?

## Data

fit20 training records (Steele et al. 2022; OSF jn6ay, CC BY 4.0): 1,978,873 cleaned member-machine-days from 22,400 members, 2010-04-09 to 2016-12-31 (the paper's window). One protocol only: one slow set to momentary failure per machine, about once a week, supervised, in fit20 studios (NL/DE). Loads are machine kg, so every number below is a *relative* change of one person's load on one machine (log ratio), never a comparison across machines. Member ids are published rounded to 7 significant digits; ids whose session numbers point to two different dates (two people sharing an id) are dropped.

Cases: 358,972 (member x machine x monthly cutoff, one random horizon of 4/8/13/26/39/52 weeks each; actual = load at the session nearest the target date, within 14 days). Targets exist only for people still training then, so every result is *conditional on still training at the target date* (survivorship, see weaknesses).

| fold | train cases | train members | test cases | test members | test cutoffs (months) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 71,591 | 3,497 | 92,569 | 5,935 | 17 |
| B | 33,235 | 1,852 | 47,025 | 2,887 | 12 |

Train and test never share a member (md5 hash split) and training targets end before the first test cutoff. Independent periods: fold A tests 17 monthly cutoffs (2015-07..2016-11) and fold B 12 (2014-07..2015-06), i.e. **two non-overlapping test windows of 12-18 months**; within a window horizons overlap, so cutoffs are not independent of each other. Intervals below are member-cluster bootstraps.

## 1. Point prediction (median of the log change)

Each candidate is fitted on train by least absolute deviation (closed-form A for a grid of tau) and scored once on test. Metric: mean |ln(actual / predicted)| in % (about the mean absolute % error).

**Fold A** (92,569 test cases, 5,935 members)

| method | fitted on train | MAE % | bias % (+ = too high) | vs no change [95% CI] |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| no change (load stays the same) | - | 8.34 | -3.14 | - |
| recent trend x horizon | - | 18.61 | +7.93 | +10.27 [+9.96, +10.59] |
| recent trend, capped at 4 weeks | - | 9.00 | -0.34 | +0.67 [+0.60, +0.73] |
| linear-log in weeks (paper's form) | b = 0.0890 | 7.52 | +0.84 | -0.82 [-0.88, -0.75] |
| DEFAULT saturating curve in weeks | A = 0.3442, tau = 10 wk | 7.25 | +0.19 | -1.08 [-1.15, -1.02] |
| saturating curve in sessions (consistency) | A = 0.3581, tau = 8 sessions | 7.23 | +0.19 | -1.10 [-1.16, -1.04] |
| curve in weeks, clock x pace^0.5 | A = 0.3460, tau = 10 wk | 7.26 | +0.12 | -1.07 [-1.13, -1.01] |
| curve in weeks, clock x pace^1 | A = 0.3446, tau = 10 wk | 7.29 | +0.03 | -1.05 [-1.11, -0.99] |

**Fold B** (47,025 test cases, 2,887 members)

| method | fitted on train | MAE % | bias % (+ = too high) | vs no change [95% CI] |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| no change (load stays the same) | - | 10.41 | -4.43 | - |
| recent trend x horizon | - | 26.61 | +11.81 | +16.20 [+15.45, +16.94] |
| recent trend, capped at 4 weeks | - | 10.78 | -1.27 | +0.37 [+0.27, +0.47] |
| linear-log in weeks (paper's form) | b = 0.0924 | 9.12 | +0.92 | -1.29 [-1.41, -1.16] |
| DEFAULT saturating curve in weeks | A = 0.3400, tau = 10 wk | 8.91 | -0.49 | -1.50 [-1.62, -1.39] |
| saturating curve in sessions (consistency) | A = 0.3530, tau = 8 sessions | 8.87 | -0.50 | -1.53 [-1.65, -1.43] |
| curve in weeks, clock x pace^0.5 | A = 0.3408, tau = 10 wk | 8.92 | -0.56 | -1.49 [-1.59, -1.38] |
| curve in weeks, clock x pace^1 | A = 0.3385, tau = 10 wk | 8.96 | -0.68 | -1.45 [-1.57, -1.35] |

Reading: the saturating curves beat doing nothing in both folds, by about 1.1 (A) and 1.5 (B) points of MAE; the trend baselines are worse than doing nothing (fit20 loads move in steps, so a recent trend over-extrapolates), and the paper's linear-log form is in between (it never plateaus, so it over-predicts experienced members). Consistency: counting training age in *sessions* (future sessions = sessions per week x horizon) is a hair better than calendar weeks: -0.019 [-0.029, -0.010] points in fold A and -0.034 [-0.053, -0.018] in fold B (member bootstrap). That is real but tiny, and it needs a complete log since the first session, so the default keeps calendar weeks (a start date is enough); slowing the weeks clock for people who train less than weekly (pace) did not help.

Fold A test by training age (weeks since first session on that machine):

| training age | cases | model MAE % | no-change MAE % | model bias % | actual median change % |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0-4 wk | 6,698 | 12.86 | 21.32 | -1.94 | +17.3 |
| 4-12 wk | 11,633 | 9.44 | 12.54 | +0.75 | +8.0 |
| 12-26 wk | 17,038 | 7.64 | 8.16 | +0.24 | +3.3 |

| 2+ yr | 15,765 | 4.93 | 4.93 | +0.61 | +0.0 |

Fold A test by horizon (weeks):

| horizon | cases | model MAE % | no-change MAE % |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 25,377 | 4.28 | 4.67 |
| 8 | 22,292 | 5.94 | 6.85 |
| 13 | 19,425 | 7.52 | 8.79 |
| 26 | 12,951 | 10.13 | 11.85 |
| 39 | 8,156 | 11.75 | 13.65 |
| 52 | 4,368 | 13.09 | 14.96 |

Fitted default (fold A train): gain = A (exp(-w/tau) - exp(-(w+h)/tau)), A = 0.3442, tau = 10 weeks: a total median gain of 41% from the first session, 93% of it within 26 weeks. Median gain still to come:

| weeks trained | next 52 weeks | next 13 weeks |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | +40.8 | +28.5 |
| 4 | +25.8 | +18.3 |
| 8 | +16.6 | +11.9 |
| 13 | +9.8 | +7.1 |
| 26 | +2.6 | +1.9 |
| 52 | +0.2 | +0.1 |

Median train residual (actual - curve, %) by group; values near 0 mean the pooled curve already fits that group:

| group | value | first 26 weeks | later |
|---|---|---|---|
| machine | Chest press | -1.47 | -0.02 |
| machine | Leg press | +1.50 | +1.37 |
| machine | Pulldown | -0.06 | -0.01 |
| sex | FEMALE | -0.19 | -0.00 |
| sex | MALE | +0.12 | -0.00 |

| current load tertile (first 26 wk, within machine) | low | +3.05 | - |
| current load tertile (first 26 wk, within machine) | mid | -0.24 | - |
| current load tertile (first 26 wk, within machine) | high | -1.06 | - |

Current ability: in the first 26 weeks, members whose load is in the lowest third for their machine and training age gained about 3% more than the curve, the highest third about 1% less (a ceiling effect, as Latella et al. 2020 found in powerlifters). Not used: absolute loads are not comparable between machines or gyms, so a user's log cannot be placed in these tertiles.

Per-machine curves (fitted on each machine's train cases, scored on its test cases):

| machine | fitted | test MAE % per-machine | test MAE % pooled |
|---|---|---|---|
| Leg press | A = 0.390, tau = 16 wk | 6.62 | 6.71 |
| Chest press | A = 0.316, tau = 7 wk | 7.71 | 7.79 |
| Pulldown | A = 0.363, tau = 8 wk | 7.20 | 7.22 |

Sex and age move the median by about 1% or less (the paper also found minimal sex and age interactions). The leg press keeps gaining a little longer than the two upper-body machines; per-machine curves change test MAE by about 0.1 point or less (table above), so the default stays pooled (a user's exercise is not one of these machines anyway).

## 2. Uncertainty bands

Quantiles (2.5..97.5%) of the train log error e = ln(actual) - ln(current) - gain, as linear functions of horizon = sqrt(h/52), novice = exp(-weeks/tau), irregular = clamp(1 - sessions per week, 0, 1) and gap = days since last session / 56 (linear quantile regression, pinball loss). Fitted on fold A train, scored once on fold A test:

| bands | pinball x100 | in 50% | in 80% | in 95% |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| horizon only | 2.382 | 54.3 | 82.7 | 96.0 |
| DEFAULT horizon + novice + irregular + gap | 2.314 | 53.5 | 82.0 | 95.8 |

Coverage on fold A test by group (target 50 / 80 / 95):

| group | cases | in 50% | in 80% | in 95% | in 80% (horizon-only bands) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| all | 92,569 | 53.5 | 82.0 | 95.8 | 82.7 |
| first 4 weeks | 6,698 | 52.2 | 79.3 | 95.7 | 57.6 |
| 1+ years | 36,171 | 60.2 | 83.2 | 95.7 | 87.6 |
| < 0.5 sessions/week | 8,902 | 52.9 | 80.9 | 95.0 | 76.5 |
| >= 1 session/week | 22,824 | 51.0 | 80.3 | 95.4 | 79.4 |
| last session > 4 weeks ago | 3,061 | 46.2 | 81.5 | 95.1 | 72.9 |
| horizon <= 8 wk | 47,669 | 54.8 | 82.4 | 96.0 | 83.4 |
| horizon >= 39 wk | 12,524 | 51.0 | 83.2 | 95.9 | 83.2 |

Consistency matters for the *spread*: people who train less than once a week get wider bands (mostly a longer upper tail: an irregular trainer's last load is a weaker guide), and a long gap since the last session widens the lower tail (detraining). The 50% band over-covers members trained 1+ years (60%): most of their sessions repeat the same load, so many actuals sit exactly on the median.

Examples (median and 80% range of the change from today's load):

| situation | median | 80% range |
|---|---|---|
| novice, weekly, 13 wk | +22.8% | +3.1% to +51.3% |
| 1 year in, weekly, 26 wk | +0.2% | -14.7% to +11.4% |
| 1 year in, every 2nd week, 26 wk | +0.2% | -16.0% to +16.0% |
| 1 year in, 6-week gap, 26 wk | +0.2% | -23.6% to +13.9% |

## 3. The model itself, end to end (data/backtest.csv)

`data/backtest.csv` holds one random fold A test case per test member (5,935 people, so rows are independent people; 17 monthly cutoffs), each with its last 12 weeks of log and the first-session date, exactly the inputs a user gives. `ballmonitor backtest strength_progress [--variant ...]` reproduces this table from config.toml (it is not refitted here).

| variant | people | MAE % | bias % | in 50% | in 80% | in 95% |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| default | 5935 | 8.08 | +0.25 | 50.2 | 81.1 | 95.6 |
| no_gain | 5935 | 9.70 | -5.16 | 48.2 | 75.7 | 94.1 |
| recent_trend | 5935 | 18.36 | +5.52 | 32.3 | 57.9 | 83.2 |
| linear_log | 5935 | 8.26 | -0.10 | 48.8 | 81.3 | 95.5 |
| consistency | 5935 | 8.08 | +0.15 | 51.9 | 80.9 | 95.5 |

Config check: config.toml matches this fit.

## Weaknesses and hindsight flags

- One protocol: one slow set to failure per machine, about weekly, supervised. Free-weight lifters, multi-set programs and people who train 3-4 times a week are not in the data; their curves may rise further and for longer (see MODEL.md literature).
- Survivorship: targets are observed only for people still training then. The prediction answers "if you keep training like this".
- Loads are machine kg in steps (load rises in increments; most sessions repeat the previous load), so the median change is often exactly 0 for experienced members.
- Two test windows (2014-15, 2015-16) from one company's studios; the 2017+ data were left out like in the paper (sensor equipment changed the recorded loads).
- No hindsight inputs: all features use sessions before the cutoff only; the target session is chosen by date, not by its value.
